stories.title: SAP adds product level emissions data to cloud services
stories.summary: SAP has made product level emissions and energy data available for selected cloud services. The methodology uses server activity and aligns with the GHG Protocol ICT Sector Guidance. The company plans to expand coverage and include more detail for AI workloads. Data is now a product feature.

stories.title: Bremenports releases first report under European SME standard
stories.summary: Bremenports has published its tenth sustainability report, titled Responsibility for the Ports of Tomorrow. For the first time, the company prepared the document in accordance with the European Voluntary Sustainability Reporting Standard for SMEs. It covers the 2024 and 2025 financial years for the port management firm.

stories.title: Ghana receives 6.57 million forest carbon credits
stories.summary: Ghana has been issued 6.57 million carbon credits for forest protection efforts across 2.5 million hectares. The credits were issued under the ART TREES standard and are the first to receive the Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market Core Carbon Principles. The country eyes $43 million.

stories.title: Indonesia and Japan Expand Forest Carbon Credit Cooperation at COP31
stories.summary: Indonesia and Japan are looking to expand their cooperation in forest-based carbon projects through the Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM), creating new opportunities for carbon finance, forest restoration, and biodiversity protection. The partnership could also help connect Indonesia’s large forest-carbon potential with Japan’s growing demand for

stories.title: Brazil projects $840 billion climate finance shortfall
stories.summary: Brazil projects climate funding will fall $840 billion short of a $1.3 trillion annual goal at COP31. While small island states press for faster cash, Western governments are prioritizing domestic security and living costs. The conference is currently focused on existing pledges rather than a new target.

stories.title: Corporate coalition to tender 1 million carbon credits in 2027
stories.summary: The Action for a Resilient Climate coalition will launch its first tender in 2027 to purchase one million tonnes of carbon credits. The group aims to reach 10 million tonnes by 2030 to advance corporate sustainability commitments. Nature-based projects like mangrove restoration are the primary focus.

stories.title: Singapore expands carbon market initiatives at COP31
stories.summary: Singapore is using the COP31 summit in Antalya to announce new grant funding for carbon projects in South-east Asia. The government aims to use carbon markets to contribute to global climate action and channel funds into developing countries. The initiatives were announced on November 12.

stories.title: Ireland joins coalition to grow carbon markets
stories.summary: Ireland has joined the Coalition to Grow Carbon Markets, a group of 15 members seeking to encourage private investment in carbon credits. The pact commits to developing markets with regulatory oversight. Critics argue that carbon credits allow businesses and countries to buy their way out of emission-reduction responsibilities.

stories.title: Indigenous leaders seek action at COP31
stories.summary: The COP31 summit in Antalya is billed as an implementation conference focused on turning previous agreements into action. Indigenous leaders, who saw historic attendance at last year's summit, are now testing whether the promises made in Brazil will translate into tangible results beyond the negotiation halls.

stories.title: COP31 Heads for Delivery Test

stories.title: Fossil fuel delegations outnumber vulnerable nations at COP31
stories.summary: More than 100 companies and industry groups linked to fossil fuels have sent delegations to COP31. According to the Kick Big Polluters Out coalition, these groups outnumber delegates from climate-vulnerable nations like Niger and Nepal. The summit is currently the largest in the event's thirty-year history.

stories.title: UN chief delivers final climate warning at COP31
stories.summary: Outgoing UN Secretary-General António Guterres used his final climate press conference to warn that peace cannot be built on a burning planet. Guterres has frequently castigated fossil fuel reliance during his tenure. He argued that natural systems must be protected to ensure a future for young people.

stories.title: Bilateral funding dominates COP31 as talks enter final week
stories.summary: Major economies are deploying capital through bilateral agreements and development banks rather than fresh public grants at COP31. While Beijing secured a renewable energy partnership with Turkey, fundamental disagreements over financial obligations remain unresolved as ministers prepare for the final week of the climate summit.

stories.title: Zero Waste Europe urges food waste action at COP31
stories.summary: Zero Waste Europe is partnering with food bank and clean air groups to push for scaled-up food waste prevention at the COP31 summit. The full report on their proposals and the conference's response to waste reduction is available to subscribers of the publication.

stories.title: Sachin Tendulkar invests in waste management firm Recykal
stories.summary: Cricket player Sachin Tendulkar has acquired a minority stake in Hyderabad-based Recykal. The investment is part of a 23 million dollar bridge funding round for the waste management technology company. The firm aims to promote responsible waste management and strengthen India's circular economy.

stories.title: Roswall confirms single point EPR reporting
stories.summary: Environment minister Romina Roswall has confirmed that the Circular Economy Act will implement a single point reporting system for Extended Producer Responsibility. The full details of the regulatory framework and its implications for member states remain available only to subscribers of the publication.

stories.title: EU industrial emissions fall as carbon revenue hits record
stories.summary: Greenhouse gas emissions from industrial installations under the EU Emissions Trading System fell 3.3 percent in 2025. During the same period, revenue from emissions allowance auctions rose 11 percent to 43.2 billion euros. The iron, steel, cement and chemical sectors led the decline in emissions.

stories.title: Algeria reviews circular economy progress at COP31
stories.summary: Environment minister Kaoutar Krikou presented Algeria's circular economy achievements at COP31 in Antalya. The minister highlighted efforts to engage youth and startups in environmental initiatives, noting that more than 6,000 economic operators are now involved in the country's push toward zero waste and methane reduction.

stories.title: Audi launches used parts business
stories.summary: Audi has established a new division called Audi Circular Solutions to facilitate the sale of used vehicle parts. The company is moving to integrate reclaimed components into its supply chain. Further details regarding the platform's operations are currently restricted by the company's website settings.

stories.title: New York landfill reaches Statue of Liberty height
stories.summary: The Seneca Meadows landfill in New York has reached 300 feet, roughly the height of the Statue of Liberty. Operators are seeking permission to increase the height further. The site now covers 350 acres of waste in the Finger Lakes region.

stories.title: Waste pickers demand role in circular economy
stories.summary: Waste pickers argue that Africa's circular economy transition requires their participation to succeed. The sector currently accounts for nearly 20 percent of global human-caused methane emissions. The UN estimates municipal solid waste will reach 3.8 billion tonnes by 2050, up from 2.1 billion in 2023.

stories.title: Government concludes Special Campaign 6.0
stories.summary: The Indian government concluded its month-long Special Campaign 6.0 on 31 October. The drive focused on e-waste management, administrative efficiency and record disposal. Originally centered on cleanliness, the initiative has expanded to include broader resource management and environmental sustainability goals across government departments.

stories.title: EU mandates recyclable packaging by 2030
stories.summary: The EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation requires all packaging to be recyclable by 2030. Mandatory shares of post-consumer recycled material will also be enforced. Companies are facing rising material costs and supply chain pressure as design for recycling shifts from a voluntary feature to a requirement.

stories.title: India and Norway partner on waste-to-resource projects
stories.summary: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research and Norwegian partners held a dialogue on waste-to-resource solutions for the construction sector. The collaboration falls under the India-Norway Green Strategic Partnership, which aims to transform industrial waste into construction materials and promote circular economy practices.

stories.title: Recycling industry seeks policy clarity
stories.summary: A draft law in Vietnam aims to treat recycled materials as goods to boost the recycling industry. The proposal includes mandatory recycling roadmaps and regulations on recycled content. Industry advocates argue that stable output markets and stronger financial mechanisms are necessary to achieve a breakthrough.

stories.title: US data center power demand outpaces grid capacity
stories.summary: US data center electricity demand has grown by 19 percent annually since 2000, while grid capacity increased by 2 percent. Data centers now account for 5 percent of total US grid capacity, up from 0.1 percent in 2000. The full report is available to subscribers.

stories.title: Touton reports 45 percent sustainable cocoa trade
stories.summary: Commodities group Touton released its annual sustainability report, noting that 45 percent of its 400,000 metric tonnes of traded cocoa and coffee were classified as sustainable. The company is currently mapping its plantations to prepare for upcoming EU deforestation regulations.

stories.title: Companies urged to align with AI data center policies
stories.summary: Following the 2026 US midterm elections, companies are being advised to align their policy agendas with increasing restrictions on AI data centers. Business leaders are encouraged to ensure trade associations support responsible buildouts as the regulatory landscape shifts in response to public concerns.

stories.title: Insurers seek seat at COP31
stories.summary: Delegates at COP31 have called for the insurance industry to participate directly in plenary sessions. The request highlights the sector's role in climate risk management. Further details regarding the conference proceedings are available only to subscribers of the publication.

stories.title: COP31 focuses on urban climate resilience
stories.summary: Over 600 CEOs and 100 national leaders met at COP31 to discuss investment in urban climate resilience. The conference prioritizes building decarbonization and early warning systems. President Murat Kurum stated that national climate commitments must translate into tangible infrastructure improvements where people live.

stories.title: Wind industry targets 4TW capacity by 2035
stories.summary: The Global Wind Energy Council launched a declaration at COP31 aiming to increase installed wind capacity to 4 terawatts by 2035. The initiative calls for closer cooperation between governments and financial institutions to unlock investment and address current barriers to project deployment.

stories.title: Panel warns of carbon removal supply shortage
stories.summary: Industry representatives at COP31 warned that companies may struggle to secure high-quality carbon removals as demand surges. Experts suggested that early offtake agreements are necessary to finance new projects. New EU certification rules are currently reshaping the market for durable removal capacity.

stories.title: Wiley reports 28 percent emissions reduction
stories.summary: Wiley released its fiscal 2026 sustainability report, claiming a 28 percent reduction in emissions since 2020. CEO Matthew Kissner described the company's approach as stewardship, focusing on protecting the integrity of knowledge while ensuring that innovation remains sustainable.

stories.title: COP31 declaration targets global scale-up of biogas
stories.summary: An international declaration launched at COP31 calls for governments to accelerate biogas and biomethane deployment. The sector aims to unlock production potential equivalent to one quarter of current natural gas demand. The declaration seeks to integrate renewable gases into existing energy markets. Gas is now renewable.

stories.title: Model law proposed to manage data center growth
stories.summary: Climate Mayors has introduced a model law to help cities manage data center siting and permitting. The organization claims data centers are moving at a scale that most local codes cannot handle. The framework aims to improve transparency and community benefits for local governments.

stories.title: Grid capacity identified as missing link for renewables
stories.summary: Professor Jairo Quirós-Tortós argues that the clean energy transition depends on grid infrastructure. Over 1,500 GW of renewable projects currently wait in connection queues globally. In Latin America and the Caribbean, curtailed clean power cost USD 7 billion in 2024. The wires are catching up.

stories.title: Nuveen launches nature-based investment vehicle
stories.summary: Nuveen Natural Capital has launched a strategy combining farmland, timberland and carbon markets into one vehicle, backed by a $100 million investment from parent company TIAA. The strategy focuses on developed markets in the United States, Australia and Europe. Nature is now an asset class.

research.title: Experimental GLP-1 drug demonstrates pain relief in people with osteoarthritis during trials
research.summary: A pooled analysis of the studies found that about two-thirds of participants receiving the drug retatrutide experienced at least a 50% reduction in knee pain, compared with 38% of those receiving a placebo
